ai.title: Putting a spotlight on AI, society, and humanity
ai.brief: MIT students are going to office hours less often. They’re spending less time working through problem sets, and with one another. Those were among the findings of MIT’s recent report on artificial intelligence and education , and they are one reason a growing number of MIT faculty are concerned about how generative AI is both changing how people work and affecting how they think, learn, and relate to one another. For the MIT Human Insight Collaborative (MITHIC), those questions have become a central focus, and MITHIC is working with collaborators across the Institute, including the Social and Ethical Responsibilities of Computing (SERC), to help MIT address them. Launched in 2024 as a strategic initiative, MITHIC brings together scholars, artists, educators, and researchers to explore the human dimensions of the defining challenges of our time. 5 million in funding.

sec.title: Apple Services Disrupted as NSA Network Goes Down and Equinor Faces Cyberattack
sec.brief: S. Banks Struggle With Outages Amid Wider Technology Disruptions Apple customers faced widespread service problems on November 17, with issues affecting iCloud, the App Store, Apple Music and AppleCare on Device. The disruption came after a week of technical failures involving major technology companies, banking services and US government networks. At the same time, Norwegian energy company Equinor disclosed a cyberattack against some of its IT systems. Apple’s System Status page reported problems with iCloud Account and Sign In, affecting all users. The issue prevented customers from signing in to their Apple accounts or caused repeated requests for their Apple ID passwords. Some users also reported difficulties activating new iPhones, suggesting that the disruption was affecting essential account services, not just individual apps. According to TechCrunch , the problems also affected the App Store, Apple Music and AppleCare on Device.
